algorithm: UniDex-VLA: a pi0-style flow-matching VLA with a Uni3D pointcloud encoder and Gemma-based backbone, predicting actions in a unified Function-Actuator-Aligned Space (FAAS) across 8 dexterous hands
hand: Inspire, Leap, Shadow, Allegro, Ability, Oymotion, XHand, Wuji (8 hands in UniDex-Dataset); real-robot eval uses Inspire, Wuji, and Oymotion hands
headline_metric: average task progress / final success rate (20 trials/task) vs. pi0 and diffusion-policy baselines
headline_value: UniDex-VLA 81.0%±12.1 avg task progress / 76.0%±17.8 final success vs. pi0 38.0%±7.4/35.0%±10.0, DP3 35.0%±17.1/30.0%±18.7, DP 29.0%±19.9/22.0%±22.5 (Fig. 11); cross-hand zero-shot transfer (Inspire-trained -> Wuji 40%, Oymotion 60% avg task progress, vs. baselines near zero)
human_data: UniDex-Dataset built from 4 existing egocentric RGB-D datasets (H2O, HOI4D, HOT3D, TACO): 9M paired image-pointcloud-action frames, 52K trajectories across 8 robot hands, produced via human-in-the-loop kinematic retargeting plus visual hand-masking/re-attachment
note_gaps: the Conclusion's stated limitation is truncated in the parsed markdown before the actual limitation text; the conditional flow-matching loss formula (Appendix A.1) is not reproduced in the parsed main-text sections read
operator_interface: human-video side: no live capture rig, converts existing egocentric RGB-D datasets (H2O, HOI4D, HOT3D, TACO) via offline retargeting; fine-tuning demonstrations collected via OpenTeleVision + dex-retargeting on an Apple Vision Pro
retargeting_objective: two-stage human-in-the-loop kinematic retargeting: an automatic PyBullet multi-end-effector IK stage aligns a 6-DoF offset between a virtual human-hand-fixed base and the real robot base to match fingertip positions (respecting joint limits, with iterative mimic-joint correction), followed by an interactive GUI stage where a human manually corrects alignment; a separate visual-alignment step masks the human hand from the pointcloud and re-renders the retargeted robot-hand mesh into the scene
